Hi!

The PCPP link you posted isn't valid (404). Could you post a permalink or just post the part list in Markdown?

Just for some perspective: the rig you have listed will get you 60 FPS on Witcher 3 @1080p at almost max settings. I have the Gigabyte gtx 970 Gaming G1 and run W3 with everything at Ultra except Nvidia Hairworks and shadows set to high. I get 60 fps with dips every one in a while. Better cards (980, 980ti, Fury X, etc) benefit you if you have a 144Hz monitor (to display >60fps) or if you're gaming at 1440p or 4k.

As far as manufacturers, I'll list by component..

  • Mobo: Asus and Gigabyte for high-end quality, ASRock for a less-expensive alternative. MSI is a popular choice as well.

  • RAM: It has little effect on overall performance (8GB is 8GB, 16 is 16). That said, the standard is 1600MHz @ the lowest CAS you can get. Anything better is great, but you won't notice much difference in everyday use.

  • HDD: Western Digital is a popular, reliable choice and the Caviar Blue is a good model. A 1TB drive will run about $50. Be sure to get a 7200RPM drive, it operates faster. The Black series is nicer, tweaked to run faster and has a longer warranty, but is more expensive. The Green drives are slower and meant to be used for backing up your system. They're reliable but not as ideal for daily use. The Reds are server drives - I don't know why

  • SSD: Samsung EVO and Crucial are good brands. Samsung has really good support for optimizing the drive as well. 120GB is acceptable, but I think the 250GB drive is a better deal.

  • Case: Aesthetic preference is a determining factor. That's what you're going to be looking at when it's all said and done. Higher quality cases (usually more expensive) will have solid materials, better airflow, dust filters, and consideration for cable management. Look for a case with USB 3.0 ports as well. NZXT and Corsair are good choices. Also, there are four major form-factors: Mini ITX, Micro ATX (mATX), Mid-Tower, and Full Tower. I listed them by size, small to large. A lot of people recommend a Mid-Tower case for your first build as there is plenty of room to work and good airflow. They are pretty big still. I kind of wish I had gone with an mATX case to be honest.

  • PSU: Use PCPP to see your estimated wattage and go a little higher than that. I don't think it's really worth it to go less than 500W though. You want a reliable brand here so your rig doesn't catch fire or explode (slight hyperbole). EVGA SuperNova and Seasonic are great choices. Corsair RM series is very good. The Corsair CX series is prevalent in the builds I see, a fine choice and a good price. You also want to get a modular or semi-modular PSU. The cables are detachable from the box so you only need to plug in the ones you're using. All the extra, unused cables clutter up a case quickly if you go non-modular.

  • CPU: If you're not on a <$500 budget, go Intel. The speed per core crushes AMD. AMD might look good on paper, but it's definitely much slower. The i5 you chose is really all you need for gaming. An i7 will only be worthwhile if you do heavy multitasking like CAD work or Photoshop or rendering.

  • GPU: As I said above, a gtx 970 will perform wonderfully at 1080p. AMD cards will be cheaper for the same performance, but they run hotter and use more power. That said, the 290x is at a great price point right now and will be better than a 970.

Hope this helps! I'm glad to answer more questions!
